title: Mural, a startup founded by former Palantir engineers, raises $15 million bid to connect banks to the emerging bot economy
detail:
Mural, a startup founded by former Palantir engineers, raises $15 million bid to connect banks to the emerging bot economy
Chris Fernandes (left) and Sinclair Toffa (right) founded Mural to help businesses manage payments across currencies and borders. · Fortune · COURTESY OF MURAL
Camila Grigera Naón
Tue, October 20, 2026 at 7:00 AM MST 3 min read
PLTR
Trade PLTR on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

The stablecoin boom has promised to make global commerce faster and cheaper by easing cross-border money transfers. But delivering on that promise remains complicated, as businesses still have to juggle banks, payment providers, and a patchwork of regulations. New York-based startup Mural wants to fix that problem by offering businesses one place to manage international payments, rather than having to piece together the system themselves. 

Cofounded by former Palantir engineers Sinclair Toffa and Chris Fernandes in 2022, Mural announced Tuesday that it has raised a $15 million Series A funding round. The startup plans to use the funds to further build out its platform, which allows customers—including payroll providers, software companies and fintechs—to rely on a single account that can hold traditional dollars, local currencies, and stablecoins.

"[We are] building this… compliant system of record that allows for businesses and fintechs to launch new financial products on top of us," Toffa, who serves as Mural's CEO, explained.

Fintech innovation has reshaped how money moves in recent years, and stablecoins have become part of that shift. These cryptocurrencies, typically designed to track the U.S. dollar, can move across borders in seconds, sometimes only for pennies in network fees. Stablecoin payments reached roughly $400 billion in the first eight months of 2026, up from the same period a year earlier, per a report from global consulting firm Alvarez & Marsal. Their use for international transfers has also grown: cross-border stablecoin flows totaled $220 billion from July 2025 through June 2026, up nearly 78% from the previous 12 months, according to blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis.

Tether, the issuer behind the USDT stablecoin, led Mural's Series A, with participation from North Island Ventures. The round brings Mural's total funding to $28 million, following a $5 million seed round in 2022 and additional pre-seed and interim financing from earlier backers. Mural declined to disclose its valuation following its latest fundraising round. 

Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said the investment also reflects a bet on AI agents becoming regular handlers of financial services.

"Those agents will need access to payment systems that operate around the clock and can reach people across the world," he told Fortune in a written statement. 

From Palantir to payments

Toffa's interest in international payments began when he visited Togo, his grandfather's home country, when he was 15 years old. His relatives there, who routinely received remittances from his father in the United States, told him that transfers could take weeks to arrive and cost as much as 20% in fees.

title: Palantir Wins Knox Federal Partnership, Gains 4%
detail:
Palantir Wins Knox Federal Partnership, Gains 4%
Michael Douglass
Mon, October 19, 2026 at 1:20 PM MST 3 min read
PLTR
QQQ
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Palantir Wins Knox Federal Partnership, Gains 4% ©yangwenshuang from Getty Images Signature and Aflo Images via Canva
Key Takeaways

Palantir shares rose 4% today after Knox Systems announced a partnership to bring commercial software into FedRAMP and IL5 federal environments.

The deal lets other companies' software reach the government through Palantir's federal accreditations, which makes Palantir more central to how agencies get new technology.

No financial terms were disclosed, and analysts already expect revenue to climb from $4.48 billion in 2025 to $8.22 billion in 2026.

The next test is the third-quarter report, which management guided to $2.16 billion to $2.164 billion of revenue.

Palantir Technologies (PLTR:NASDAQ) shares are up 4% today after Knox Systems announced a partnership, before Monday's open, to get commercial software into the government's most tightly secured clouds.

That wins back part of Friday's 7% drop, which pushed the stock into a correction. (Tech is having a good day, too: the QQQ QQQ:NASDAQ is up nearly 2%.)

What exactly happened

Knox, which is private, runs a managed federal cloud and says it can get software makers FedRAMP authorization in 90 days or less. It already hosts more than 100 AI and enterprise applications, for customers including Adobe (ADBE:NASDAQ), Sierra and Armis.

Palantir has already helped software companies deploy to federal agencies on its own accredited infrastructure, IL5 environments included. Put the two together, and a software maker gets one route from authorization to deployment.

As Knox CEO Irina Denisenko said in the press release: "Knox exists to get the best software in the world to the government faster, and to protect it once it's there."

Neither company disclosed financial terms.

Palantir becomes the on-ramp

Those accreditations are the hard part for any software maker selling to the Pentagon, and this deal puts Palantir's to work for other companies' products.

It also lands on top of a government business that's already flying. Palantir's U.S. government revenue rose 90% year over year to $809 million in Q2 2026, out of $1.94 billion in total revenue.

Analysts expect revenue to nearly double again this year, to $8.22 billion, and to reach $17.9 billion by 2028…

Palantir Technologies (PLTR): revenue, actual and consensus estimates, $ billions, fiscal 2023–2028 (TIKR)

With no terms disclosed, there's nothing in today's news for analysts to add to those estimates yet.

The multiple already came down

At Friday's close, Palantir traded at 98x forward earnings. That's a touch below its five-year average of 103x and far from the 270x it hit in October 2025…

Palantir Technologies (PLTR): forward (NTM) P/E, last 5 years (TIKR)

Today's move puts it right back at that average. That's still a rich price, so the next real test is the third quarter, which management guided to $2.16 billion to $2.164 billion of revenue.

title: Palantir Stock Is Near a Record High. Should Investors Sell?
detail:
Palantir Stock Is Near a Record High. Should Investors Sell?
Lawrence Nga, The Motley Fool
Mon, October 19, 2026 at 12:20 PM MST 5 min read
PLTR
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

For Palantir Technologies (NASDAQ: PLTR) shareholders, the hardest part of investing may not be buying the stock. It may be deciding when to sell.

After a tremendous run, Palantir is trading near its all-time high. Investors who bought early may be sitting on substantial gains, while newer shareholders may wonder whether the best returns are already behind them.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

My view: Don't sell Palantir simply because its stock has soared. But don't hold it blindly, either. Existing shareholders should reassess three things: the company's growth prospects, the return its current valuation can deliver, and the amount of their portfolio tied up in the stock.

A great business can remain a great investment for years. But the price you pay, or continue holding at, still matters.

Image source: Getty Images.
Palantir's business gives shareholders a reason to stay

Palantir's recent results show why investors are optimistic. In the second quarter of 2026, revenue jumped 93% year over year to $1.94 billion. U.S. commercial revenue surged 149% to $764 million, while U.S. government revenue grew 90% to $809 million. Adjusted operating margin reached 62%, and management raised its full-year revenue growth guidance to 82%.

These aren't just impressive growth rates; they instead suggest Palantir is turning demand for artificial intelligence (AI) into substantial revenue while maintaining strong profitability. But strong operating performance doesn't guarantee strong stock returns, which brings us to the more difficult question.

Is future growth already priced in?

Palantir's valuation leaves investors with high expectations to meet. On Oct. 15, 2026, the stock closed at $200.50, giving the company a market capitalization of approximately $482 billion. Its trailing price-to-earnings ratio was around 171.

At that valuation, investors aren't merely expecting Palantir to succeed. They're paying a substantial premium for continued success. Suppose Palantir keeps growing but eventually trades at a lower earnings multiple. The stock could deliver disappointing returns, even if the business performs well, but if growth also slows, the pressure could be even greater.

This is the risk existing shareholders must weigh against the possibility of further gains. The question isn't whether Palantir can become a much bigger company, but whether its future earnings can grow enough to justify today's price.

What Happened?

A number of stocks jumped in the morning session after retreating yields and dip-buying supported a relief rebound following the previous session's sharp drawdown.

The bounce follows a pullback across cloud vendors, triggered by fears that aggressive artificial intelligence capital budgets are crowding out traditional software spending. Scrutiny escalated after CNBC reported that Anthropic generated $16.8 billion in third-quarter revenue, fueling concern that enterprise technology wallets are shifting toward foundation model providers at the expense of established business workflows.

Software valuations experience immediate multiple compression when sovereign borrowing benchmarks climb or budget allocations stall. With the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield receding, per CNBC reporting, lower discount rates offered tangible relief to high-multiple subscription models.

The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks.

title: Why Palantir Technologies Stock Rallied Today
detail:
Why Palantir Technologies Stock Rallied Today
Danny Vena, CPA, The Motley Fool
Mon, October 19, 2026 at 9:51 AM MST 3 min read
PLTR
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Palantir Technologies (NASDAQ:PLTR) stock was sharply higher Monday morning, gaining as much as 5.9%. As of 12:19 p.m. ET, the stock was still up 5.5%.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

The catalyst that sent the data-mining and artificial intelligence (AI) software specialist higher was a new partnership that expands the availability of its technology.

Image source: Getty Images.

More was to access Palantir

In a press release that dropped Monday morning, Palantir announced a new partnership with Knox Systems, one of the world's largest Federal and Department of Defense (DoD) managed cloud providers. The collaboration "ensures mission-critical applications have access to the most secure infrastructure possible, while still being able to deploy their product on their schedule, at the fastest pace possible."

The partnership brings together Palantir's leading data mining and AI platform and Knox's managed federal cloud computing platform. Together, the pair will help customers accelerate their acceptance into the Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program (FedRAMP), "getting the best technology into the hands of the warfighter and the U.S. Government," according to the release.

Palantir's AI solutions already help consolidate and process battlefield data in real time, identify and track enemy threats, and coordinate responses. FedRAMP and Impact Level 5 are two of the strictest federal certification standards. This partnership helps accelerate software deployments in these environments more quickly, getting the company's solutions to more warfighters more quickly.

Recent concerns about the future of AI adoption have weighed on Palantir, though the stock still appears pricey at 83 times next year's expected earnings. However, thanks to Palantir's triple-digit profit growth, the stock's price/earnings-to-growth (PEG) ratio comes in at 0.5, when any number less than 1 is the standard for an undervalued stock.

That's why Palantir stock is a buy.
